extracted.intended_audience: bibliographers, textual editors, and scholars of early-modern English literature
extracted.subtask_description: Annotated bibliographic catalogue and critical notes on seventeenth-century 'characters' (short satirical/descriptive pieces), recording imprints, contents, provenance, editions, and editorial corrections. Aimed at documenting and describing editions and their textual details for scholarly use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve original orthography in extracts
rubrics_metrics.description: In the extracts made from the foregoing series of Characters, the original orthography has been most scrupulously attended to, in order to assist in shewing the progress and variation of the English language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reproducing historical texts for scholarly purposes, retain original spelling and orthographic forms rather than modernizing, and note this editorial policy explicitly so readers understand the transcription choices and can use them to study language change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide full bibliographic imprint and format details
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry records title, imprint (printer/publisher and place), year (when given), and format designation (e.g., 12mo, 4to), and often pagination: e.g., 'Picturae loquentes... London: Printed by T. Coles, &c. 1631. 12mo.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cataloguing entries should include complete bibliographic information (title, imprint, date, format/size, pagination) to enable identification and verification of physical copies; note variant impressions and publisher shops when known.

rubrics_metrics.name: List contents or enumerated 'characters' for works
rubrics_metrics.description: For works composed of 'characters' the contents are enumerated (e.g., 'The Original Characters are: 1. The world. 2. An old man. ... 26. A gentleman's house in the countrey.'), often with additions in later editions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a contents list (even if only titles/headings) for multi-part works so that the internal structure and scope are clear; indicate additions or differences between editions (e.g., 'The Additions to the second Edition are...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Record provenance, holdings, and references to collections and prior bibliographers
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries note where copies are held and cite prior bibliographic authorities or catalogues (e.g., 'A copy of this rare volume is in the possession of Mr. Douce'; references to 'Censura Literaria', 'British Museum', 'Bodleian', sale catalogues, and other bibliographers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate known library or private holdings and cite earlier scholarship or sale catalogues to document the work's transmission and enable readers to trace physical copies and earlier commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note reprints, editions, and cross-references to related works
rubrics_metrics.description: The catalogue records reprints and later editions and cross-references similar or derivative works (e.g., 'A second edition in 1635'; 'Reprinted in the Harleian Miscellany'; 'See Brand's Sale Catalogue').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document edition history and reprints, and cross-reference related or derivative items to situate a work within its publishing and reception history; point out when items are reprinted in miscellanies or anthologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide errata, editorial corrections, and explanatory notes
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'Additional Notes and Corrections' section enumerates emendations to text and readings (e.g., 'Page 2, line 18, for _ports_ read _sports_.'), explains editorial decisions and lacunae, and apologizes for errors introduced by distance from the press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an errata/corrections section and explanatory footnotes to record identified errors, suggested emendations, textual variants, and editorial rationale; be transparent about limitations and invite reader corrections.
